svg.title: Four medical emergencies linked to MDMA
svg.desc: Overheating: MDMA interferes with temperature regulation; combined with exertion in a hot, crowded setting, core temperature can climb past 105 degrees Fahrenheit, leading to muscle breakdown, kidney and liver failure, brain swelling and death. Dangerously low sodium: MDMA increases antidiuretic hormone release, causing fluid retention; combined with drinking large amounts of water, sodium can fall far enough to cause seizures, brain swelling and coma. Serotonin syndrome: combining MDMA with SSRIs, other antidepressants or additional serotonergic drugs raises the risk of a potentially life-threatening reaction. Cardiovascular strain: rapid heart rate, high blood pressure and arrhythmias are common in acute toxicity, and risk rises sharply when an unknown stimulant adulterant is stacked on top. If someone is confused, extremely hot, vomiting, having a seizure, or unresponsive, call 911. Poison Control: 1-800-222-1222.
